text:
Alex K: Heads-up — while testing the onboarding sampleapp I hit a weird parsing hang: client stalls for ~15s and then the node SDK emits 'unexpected EOF'. Repro steps on a slow link (emulated 200ms jitter).

Maria S: ugh, can you paste the raw stream?

Alex K: sure. here's the tail (copied from tcpdump):
```
data: {"id":"tok1","delta":"Hel"}


data: {"id":"tok1","delta":"lo"}


:

data: {"id":"tok1","delta":"!"}


```
notice the extra blank line+colon between fragments — looks like a suppressed keepalive line got merged?

Ben P: hmm. colon-only lines are keepalive per older SSE clients, but our parser treats a lone `:\n` as a no-op. Could the proxy be coalescing frames so the parser gets `\n\n:\n\n` mid-fragment?

Sam R: we've seen similar when gzip+streaming and slow consumers cause chunk boundaries to shift. The SDK's state machine expects `\n\n` to mark event boundary; if keepalive lands in the middle of a data payload the reassembly logic can miscount delimiters.

Maria S: can you repro with the sampleapp + `tc` network shaping? if so, file a minimal test so we can automate.

Alex K: repro script attached in thread gist (quick):
```
# emulate slow link
sudo tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 200ms 50ms distribution normal
# run sampleapp pointing at local proxy
node sampleapp/stream-demo.js --url http://localhost:8080/stream
```
Behavior: client prints partial tokens then stops, no reconnect. After ~15s the SDK throws `Error: stream aborted (unexpected EOF)`.

Ben P: quick fix idea: tolerate colon-only keepalive anywhere inside reassembly; treat `:\n` as boundary-feedback but do not swallow the adjacent `\n`. Also increase the chunk-buffer lookahead for up to 2 delimiter permutations (`\n\n`, `\n:\n`, `:\n\n`). I'll sketch a patch.

Sam R: also add test where a payload is split across writes like `\"Hel` then `lo\"` with a keepalive injected between. We should assert final JSON still forms.

Maria S: FYI -- can we also log last-event-id handling? In one run `Last-Event-ID` header was absent and resume token was in a subsequent chunk; SDK refused to resume.

Alex K: yep saw that. I patched the sampleapp to surface `lastEventId` on reconnect attempts — pushing a PR to the sampleapp repo after I confirm patch stability.

ci-bot: ci/sampleapp-stream-demo #42 started (patch: ben/keepalive-tolerance) :gear:

Ben P: will document the edgecase in the SDK issue and add a fallback: if reconnect is due to `unexpected EOF`, try immediate lightweight resume using last seen event id. Not a full rollback but a best-effort.

Alex K: huge thanks. This was a nasty gotcha for new users — onboarding guide should call out `tc` network tests and the keepalive coalescing caveat.

Maria S: agreed, add a short note to devex onboarding doc and a runnable test in the sampleapp so we catch regressions.

Sam R: moving this to a follow-up ticket: DX-3585 (streaming: keepalive/coalesced-chunk tolerance).
